previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: James, a 60-year-old man with a history of alcohol use disorder, COPD, tobacco use, and chronic pain from prior injuries, was admitted for shortness of breath and alcohol intoxication. He was found hypoxic on room air with oxygen saturation of 82%, which improved with supplemental oxygen. Evaluation revealed mild COPD exacerbation and minimal atelectasis on chest X-ray, but no pneumonia. He was treated with steroids, antibiotics, and bronchodilators, and successfully managed for alcohol withdrawal using CIWA-guided diazepam, with symptoms improving over the hospital stay. His hypernatremia resolved with IV fluids, and lower extremity skin abrasions were managed with wound care. He expressed a strong desire to remain sober and was discharged to extended care with a plan to establish outpatient follow-up, restart inhalers, continue a short Valium taper, and address chronic pain and methadone reinitiation as an outpatient.
